text: The fatal night, a few moments later: the clang Helen hears, which Holmes reads as Dr. Roylott hastily closing his safe upon the snake
why: ¶249 states Holmes's reading that the clang Helen heard was Roylott closing the safe on the snake, following her account of the clang after the whistle.

text: Half an hour later: the creature hisses, a very gentle sound like a small jet of steam from a kettle
why: ¶236 describes the gentle steam-like sound after half an hour of waiting, and ¶249 says Holmes heard the creature hiss.

text: That instant: Holmes attacks the creature with his cane at the bell-pull
why: ¶236 states that Holmes sprang up, struck a match and lashed furiously with his cane at the bell-pull at that moment.

text: Next day, travelling back: Holmes tells of the chair, the safe, the milk and the whipcord, and of the clang
why: ¶247–249 say they travelled back next day and Holmes explains the chair, safe, milk, whipcord and clang.

text: Before Holmes inspects it: Dr. Roylott has been in the habit of standing on his chair to reach the ventilator
why: ¶249 states that inspecting the chair showed Roylott had been in the habit of standing on it to reach the ventilator.

text: In Dr. Roylott's chamber: the safe, the saucer of milk and the loop of whipcord dispel Holmes's last doubts
why: ¶249 says the safe, saucer of milk and loop of whipcord finally dispelled Holmes's remaining doubts.

text: Why did Julia strike a light? — she heard the snake hiss in the room
id: q.why_match=she heard the snake hiss in the room
why: The story never says Julia heard a hiss; the only hiss is heard by Holmes during his night watch, after Julia's death.

text: Why did the whistle sound just as Holmes struck the light?
why: ¶238 reports the whistle sounding at the instant Holmes struck the light, so the plain question is raised by the text.

text: Why did the whistle sound just as Holmes struck the light? — he saw the light through the ventilator and called the snake home
id: q.whistle_at_match=he saw the light through the ventilator and called the snake home
why: ¶229 has Holmes warn that Roylott would see the light through the ventilator, and ¶249 says Roylott trained the snake to return when summoned, so the possibility is one the story gives reason to consider.

text: Why did the whistle sound just as Holmes struck the light? — it was already time for the recall, and the match only happened to coincide
id: q.whistle_at_match=it was already time for the recall, and the match only happened to coincide
why: Julia's account and ¶249 establish a regular whistle at a set hour that Roylott chose, so a coincidence with the match is a possibility the story gives reason to consider.
